text:
The defending Stanley Cup champions are playing like it on the other side of the world. Carolina beat Seattle 4-1 in Helsinki on Thursday in the first game of the NHL Global Series Finland, with Sebastian Aho scoring twice in his home country, ten years to the day after his first NHL goal, against the same goalie, Philipp Grubauer (as NHL.com's Tom Gulitti noted). The Hurricanes outshot the Kraken 30-13, and Seattle's only goal came on its only shot of the third period. Carolina has won three straight, outscoring teams 18-6, and the chances back it: 59% of the expected goals, our measure of chance quality, in those games.

The bigger news may be who's back. Jordan Staal, last spring's Conn Smythe winner, has missed 14 games with a calf injury, and Gulitti reported this morning that the signs point to him returning, with Alexander Nikishin coming in on defense. Pyotr Kochetkov, who backed up Brandon Bussi on Thursday, is our projected starter: 9.8 goals better than expected this season. Jackson Blake carries a ten-game point streak, Logan Stankoven has 14 points in his last ten, and Mark Jankowski is one of our Sleepers, a third-liner whose shots have been more dangerous than 97% of depth forwards'.

Seattle came to Finland with Kaapo Kakko's homecoming and leaves needing something to show for it. Coach Lane Lambert told NHL.com his team didn't play to its structure on Thursday, and the Kraken have 45% of the expected goals at five on five this season. Jared McCann is out until January, Joey Daccord has stopped .865 over his last five starts, and rookie Jagger Firkus may make his NHL debut. The bright spot is Berkly Catton, ten points in ten games, though our numbers say bounces have helped.

Puck drop is 1 p.m. Eastern. Our numbers have Carolina at 3.77 expected goals to Seattle's 2.38, and the Hurricanes at better than 99% to make the playoffs. Seattle sits at 29%.
headline: Hurricanes chase a Helsinki sweep, Staal may return
